memory_candidates.content: When a task's own net-size contribution must be measured in a repo under heavy concurrent multi-task activity, a raw before/after corpus-wide instrument reading (e.g. a line-count probe) is unusable once concurrent sibling-task drift exceeds the task's own signal. The immune alternative: grep commit messages for the task's own marker (e.g. 'task N'), then for each matching commit run `git show --numstat <sha>` against its own parent (never against the task's first/last commit directly, which would include every interleaving foreign commit), restricted to the relevant path populations, and sum. Each commit's diff is inherently isolated from concurrent work by git's own commit model, so the sum is exact regardless of how many other tasks landed commits in the same window. Cross-validate against a hand-sum of each phase's own git-diff-based closing-note figure if available.

A net-deletion acceptance criterion on a multi-phase refactor task can be defeated by its own internal structure even when every individual phase is honest: infrastructure/extraction phases that declare themselves net-positive in advance (promising a later phase will pay the cost back) can accumulate faster than the payback phases actually realize, especially when later phases keep adding further infrastructure (classification, selection, fixture-sharing) without a correspondingly scaled migration phase to absorb it. The fix is not to forbid net-positive phases (sometimes the only honest path to a shared, reusable mechanism) but to track a running total continuously and treat a growing positive total as a stop-and-reassess signal before authorizing the next infrastructure phase, rather than deferring all reconciliation to the task's final measurement phase.

user_decision.question: Phase 20's final, git-history-anchored net accounting found this task's own measured contribution is NET-TOTAL +1,219 lines (NET-PROD +498, NET-TEST +1,402, NET-MD -681) -- missing the retained -10,000-line net-deletion floor by 11,219 lines and landing net-positive overall, even though Phases 6-11 and 16-19 each individually delivered real, verified negative net. The shortfall is caused by infrastructure phases (3, 4, 12, 13, 14, 16) whose declared-in-advance net-positive cost exceeded the realized payback from the migration/dedup phases that followed them. How should this task close?
options: Accept the measured result as this task's final close (mark [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] at the task level) and file a new, separately-chartered follow-up task to migrate the remaining unmigrated test suites onto the shared harness (the largest remaining realizable NET-TEST payback) and to fix the project-number-inuse.sh test-fixture gap found in gate 8
Charter an immediate continuation within this same task (a Phase 21+) to keep migrating suites until NET-TOTAL turns negative, rather than closing now

Revise the retained -10,000 floor itself, on the grounds that four independent measurement rounds (the dispatch's estimate, the Phase 2 derivation, Phase 15's -2,800 fallback, and now this -- now wrong-signed -- result) have each found it unreachable from the next-enumerated source of volume
